newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Indonesia will launch a new national car in 1998 produced by the Strategic Industry Body (BPIS), a department of the Research and Technology Ministry. The 'Maleo' will cost 25 million rupiah ($10,785) including tax and will be made using 68 percent local components with British and Australian technology.

Shareholders of Indonesian tyre producer PT Gajah Tunggal yesterday approved a rights issue worth 792 billion rupiah ($341.7 million). The firm, which already produces 35 percent of Indonmesia's car tyres, is planning to expand its production.

U.S.-based Business Software Alliance (BSA) said on Tuesday that Indonesia had made progress in reducing computer software piracy. Indonesia is still the world's worst offender, however, with 99 percent of software still illegal, said BSA vice president David Sigler.

Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), has been ordered to close down her new headquarters before Thursday. East Jakarta Mayor Colonel Sudarsono said in a letter dated Monday that the new headquarters is illegal because it is in a residential area.

The government will not intervene in the findings of Indonesia's official human rights body on the July 27 riots, State Secretary Murdiono said on Tuesday. The National Commission on Human Rights plans to finalise its report by early October. Previously, the government has asked the commission to prove its claim that 74 people were missing following the riots.

The government will later this year tender contacts for work on the Natuna natural gas fields, Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie said on Tuesday. Habibie said work would begin in 1998 to turn the islands into a centre for natural gas liquefaction.
